cards.front: When surgical treatment of a hip fracture is delayed >4 days , the 30-day, 90-day, and 1-year mortality significantly increases.
cards.extra: Moran et al (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15741611/) studied 2660 elderly patients who underwent surgical treatment of a hip fracture to determine whether a delay in surgery affects postoperative mortality. The 30-day mortality for patients for whom the surgery had been delayed for more than 4 days was 10.7%, compared to 7.3% in those delayed 1-4 days. The group delayed >4 days also had significantly increased mortality at 90 days and 1 year.
